tagline: A quiet little town that's the oldest in the North
introHtml:
Lamphun is a small town just half an hour's drive from Chiang Mai, but the feel is completely different. It used to be the city of Hariphunchai, so there are old temples and remnants of the city wall you can wander around without fighting anyone for space.

Most people visit Lamphun as a day trip — pay respects at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, walk the market, and grab some longan if you come during fruit season. But if you stay a little longer, you'll find weaving villages and rice fields that are still calm and quiet.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable (August fills the whole town with longan)

highlights.name: Wat Phra That Hariphunchai
highlights.blurb: An ancient temple in the heart of town and the soul of Lamphun — northerners consider it a place you should visit at least once in your life.

highlights.name: Hariphunchai Old Town
highlights.blurb: Traces of the city wall and moat from Queen Chamadevi's time. You can stroll around the old town easily in a single morning.

highlights.name: Lamphun longan
highlights.blurb: Lamphun is the most famous longan region in Thailand. In August fruit season the whole town fills up with longan orchards and longan souvenirs.

highlights.name: Nong Chang Khuen–Wiang Yong weaving villages
highlights.blurb: Lamphun's long-standing source of brocade silk and cotton weaving. You can buy handwoven cloth right in the community.

highlights.name: Queen Chamadevi Monument
highlights.blurb: The first monarch who founded the city of Hariphunchai — a figure Lamphun locals revere and tie closely to the town's history.

highlights.name: Ban Pa Sang
highlights.blurb: An old district with antique wooden shophouses, cotton-cloth shops, and the kind of small-town atmosphere that's getting hard to find.

foodScene.name: Khao soi and nam ngiao
foodScene.note: Staple northern dishes you can find all over town. Several old shops in central Lamphun have been around a long time.

foodScene.name: Longan and longan products
foodScene.note: Fresh longan, dried longan, longan juice, even longan ice cream — the signature souvenir of the province.

foodScene.name: Khanom jeen nam ngiao
foodScene.note: A popular northern breakfast — rice noodles topped with savory nam ngiao broth, eaten with fresh veggies and pork crackling.

foodScene.name: Sai ua, khaep mu, nam phrik num
foodScene.note: Northern snacks and a full northern spread — find them at morning markets and souvenir shops in town.

foodScene.name: Lamphun noodles
foodScene.note: Old noodle shops in town that locals have eaten at for years — simple, homey flavors.

foodScene.name: Cafes in the old town and out by the rice fields
foodScene.note: Lately small cafes have opened in the old town and beside the rice fields, using highland coffee and a quiet setting.

foodScene.name: Lamphun morning market
foodScene.note: Fresh food, ready-made northern dishes, and seasonal fruit at easygoing prices.

attractions.name: Wat Phra That Hariphunchai
attractions.blurb: Lamphun's most important temple, with a golden bell-shaped chedi and an old gateway in the center of town.

attractions.name: Wat Chamadevi (Wat Ku Kut)
attractions.blurb: An ancient temple with a square-tiered chedi in the Hariphunchai style — architecture that's rare to see.

attractions.name: Hariphunchai National Museum
attractions.blurb: Holds Hariphunchai- and Lanna-era artifacts, telling the old city's story all in one place.

attractions.name: Queen Chamadevi Monument
attractions.blurb: A key landmark in the center of town honoring the founder of Hariphunchai; people come to pay respects.

attractions.name: Ku Chang–Ku Ma
attractions.blurb: Old ruins believed to be the tombs of Queen Chamadevi's royal war elephant and horse.

attractions.name: Nong Chang Khuen weaving village
attractions.blurb: A community weaving brocade silk and cotton — you can watch the weaving and buy cloth straight from the makers.

attractions.name: Doi Khun Tan National Park
attractions.blurb: Forested hills and the Khun Tan railway tunnel, the longest in Thailand, with hiking trails and campsites.

attractions.name: Phra Borommathat Doi Koeng–Pa Sang district rice fields
attractions.blurb: Outskirts that are still rice fields and longan orchards — a quiet, easy drive on a relaxed day.

itineraryIdeas: Lamphun 1 day — pay respects at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and walk the old town
Lamphun 2D1N — old temples and weaving villages
